message: Can you look at this ECG? I think it's normal, right?
reply:
**I wouldn’t call this clearly normal.** From the image:

- The rhythm appears to be **sinus rhythm, around 70–80 beats/minute**, with narrow QRS complexes.
- There are **prominent electrical voltages** in the chest leads and **mild ST-segment depression**, particularly in leads I and aVL.
- This combination can occur with **left ventricular hypertrophy** (thickening of the heart’s main pumping chamber), but the ECG alone cannot confirm that. ST changes also need assessment in the context of symptoms and previous ECGs. [ECG interpretation reference](https://www.merckmanuals.com/professional/cardiovascular-disorders/cardiovascular-tests-and-procedures/electrocardiography)

**If you currently have chest pain, shortness of breath, sweating, or feel faint, seek emergency care now.** This image cannot rule out a heart attack. [Heart attack symptoms](https://www.cdc.gov/heart-disease/about/heart-attack.html)

If you feel well, arrange a clinician review, including a blood-pressure check and comparison with an older ECG; an echocardiogram may be appropriate.

How old are you, why was this ECG taken, and are you having any symptoms?
